public_rationale: Coxon's publicity and international discussion are documented. The records make Zitron's account plausible, but do not establish how much public discussion changed because of Coxon. Calling international coverage alone proof of entry into the global zeitgeist would make the result depend too heavily on an evaluator-defined threshold.
limitations: Public discussion can be widespread without appearing in polling.
Failure to locate measurements does not establish that Coxon had little influence.

statement.excerpt: In the end, it doesn’t really matter, because even though most of the media mostly jumped at their own shadow, the sheer volume of traffic to Coxon’s tweet and his endless media interviews have now moved the idea of the need for a “global AI slowdown” into the global zeitgeist.
statement.document_title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

from_speaker: the sheer volume of traffic to Coxon’s tweet
the need for a “global AI slowdown”
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that Coxon's publicity materially brought coordinated AI slowdown proposals into widespread international public discussion by the post date.
This does not require majority support for a slowdown or Coxon being the sole cause.
The relevant episode is the publicity preceding September 14, 2026. The supplied text does not date its beginning.
The description of media overreaction is treated as evaluative framing, not a separately measurable assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous international coverage and evidence of audience attention show a substantial increase in public discussion attributable to Coxon's tweet and interviews.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show no substantial broadening of discussion, or establish that the claimed change preceded Coxon's publicity and was not materially affected by it.
